# Acme Claude Code marketplace

This is the **org data repo** of Acme: a Claude Code plugin marketplace (`acme`), the catalog metadata that describes its plugins, the profiles developers start Claude Code with, and the CI that checks and publishes all of it. It is managed with [ccshelf](https://github.com/yorch/ccshelf). It was generated by `ccshelf catalog init`.

## Layout

```
.claude-plugin/marketplace.json    the native marketplace; hand-written
plugins/<name>/                    plugin source: .claude-plugin/plugin.json, skills/, hooks/, .mcp.json, README.md
catalog/plugins/<name>.toml        one sidecar per plugin: owner, status and when to use it
profiles/<name>.toml               profile manifests (a set of plugins and MCP servers per role)
bundles/profile-<name>/            GENERATED by "ccshelf compile": one dependency-only plugin per profile
ccshelf.toml                       org configuration: lint rules, catalog settings, protected plugins
.github/CODEOWNERS                 who reviews what
.github/workflows/                 validate (pull requests), catalog (publish on merge), release (tags)
```

## Set up (once)

- [ ] **Pin ccshelf in the workflows.** `validate.yml` and `catalog.yml` call the `yorch/ccshelf/action`. Replace the all-zero commit SHA with the full 40-character commit SHA of the ccshelf release you chose, keep its tag in the trailing comment, set `version:` to the same release, then delete the "Refuse to run until ccshelf is pinned" step. Prefer a commit that already holds the `action/pins.txt` line for your version: the binary is then pinned by the commit alone. Optionally set the repository variable `CCSHELF_SHA256_LINUX_AMD64` to the archive hash from the release's `checksums.txt`.
- [ ] **Replace every `TODO(ccshelf)`** (in `catalog/plugins/*.toml` and in marketplace descriptions). `ccshelf lint` lists them as warnings (CAT048) until they are gone.
- [ ] **Protect the repository.** Require code-owner review on the default branch, protect `v*` tags (block updates and deletion) and limit the `github-pages` environment to the default branch. `.github/` is owned by the platform team so that plugin teams cannot change workflows or CODEOWNERS.
- [ ] **Decide who the platform owners are.** `@acme/platform` own everything that runs code on developer machines or shapes the catalog: hooks, MCP servers, plugin manifests, profiles, workflows and this configuration.
- [ ] **Choose which plugins nobody may mask.** List them under `[protect]` in `ccshelf.toml`.

## Add a plugin

1. Create `plugins/<name>/` with `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` (`name`, `description`, `author`), a `README.md` and your skills. Use kebab-case names. Put hooks in `hooks/hooks.json` and MCP servers in `.mcp.json`, not inline in `plugin.json`, so that the ownership rules apply.
2. List it in `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` with `"source": "./plugins/<name>"` and a description of at least 30 characters.
3. Add `catalog/plugins/<name>.toml` with at least `owner` and `status` (`active`, `experimental` or `deprecated`). `ccshelf catalog init` writes a stub for every listed plugin; run it again to get stubs for new ones, it never changes existing files.
4. Add `/plugins/<name>/ @your-team` to `.github/CODEOWNERS` **above** the platform rules for hooks and manifests (the last matching line wins).
5. Open a pull request. CI runs `ccshelf lint`, `ccshelf compile --check` and a catalog preview.

## Profiles and the catalog

- A **profile** is a named set of plugins, MCP servers and session defaults. ccshelf has no built-in profiles: the roles are your choice. Put them in `profiles/<name>.toml` and run `ccshelf compile` to regenerate `bundles/`, then commit the result.
- The **catalog** is a static site and a `CATALOG.md` built from the marketplace and the sidecars: `ccshelf catalog build --out dist/catalog`. CI builds it on every pull request and publishes it from the default branch.

## Everyday commands

```
ccshelf lint                          check the marketplace, sidecars, ownership and profiles
ccshelf compile --check               fail when committed bundles differ from the profiles
ccshelf catalog build --out dist/catalog
ccshelf search <words>                search the catalog
```

Documentation: <https://github.com/yorch/ccshelf>.
